history.change: NLRB decides Cemex: after a card majority, the employer must recognize the union or file for an election within 2 weeks.
The 6th Circuit strikes it down (Brown-Forman). Not reliable in MI, OH, KY or TN.
GC memo 26-04 lists Cemex among the decisions the General Counsel wants reversed.

plain_summary: After a card majority asks for recognition, the employer must recognize the union or file for an election within 2 weeks.
rule: Cemex (2023): recognize or file within 2 weeks
what_to_tell_workers: Don't plan on a bargaining order. Build a majority big enough to win an election anyway.
where_it_applies: All circuits except the 6th (MI, OH, KY, TN)

history.change: The General Counsel has filed to overturn it.

plain_summary: Workers can't be forced to attend anti-union meetings; the employer must say attendance is voluntary.
what_to_tell_workers: Assume mandatory anti-union meetings are coming. Prepare coworkers in advance.

plain_summary: Employers can't predict closure or retaliation because workers unionize, unless they can prove they'd do it anyway.
what_to_tell_workers: Expect "we might close" talk. Teach the answer.

history.change: Targeted. Regions have been told to deprioritize rule-only cases.

plain_summary: Workplace rules are judged by how a worker would read them; rules that chill Section 7 activity are unlawful.
what_to_tell_workers: Talking about pay and conditions is still protected. Don't count on a handbook rule being thrown out.

plain_summary: Employers can't offer severance that forbids workers from talking about the job or the severance itself.
what_to_tell_workers: Talking about pay and conditions is still protected.

history.change: Rejected by several appeals courts; targeted for reversal.

plain_summary: Illegal firings can bring direct or foreseeable damages, like credit and search costs, on top of back pay.
what_to_tell_workers: If you're fired illegally, expect back pay and reinstatement, slowly.

citation: NLRB GC Memo 26-01 (Dec 23, 2025); applies to charges filed after Oct 1, 2025

history.change: Since late 2025, evidence (timeline, witnesses, documents) is due within 2 weeks of filing a ULP charge. TODO(verify): exact effective date.

Verified: GC 26-01 requires charging parties to e-file a chronological timeline, relevant documentation, and a witness list with contact info within two weeks of docketing. Failure may mean dismissal for lack of cooperation.

plain_summary: Since late 2025, the timeline, witnesses and documents behind a ULP charge are due within 2 weeks of filing.
rule: ULP charge intake: evidence due within 2 weeks
what_to_tell_workers: Keep notes from day one, on a personal device.

history.change: In 2015, GC Memo 15-08 allowed e-signature authorization cards with specific required fields.
GC 25-05 targeted the previous GC's memos; the published rescission lists don't include 15-08. TODO(verify) against the memo text.

plain_summary: Authorization cards may be signed electronically, with required fields: name, contact, phone, authorization language, date, employer.
what_to_tell_workers: Sign cards through the union's process.

history.change: Rule effective: faster hearings, no 20-business-day wait before the election.
No rescission published as of this date; management-side firms expect the Board to reverse it.

plain_summary: Hearings are scheduled faster and the 20-business-day wait between the direction of election and the election is gone.
what_to_tell_workers: Elections can come fast after filing. Have your majority and your inoculation done before you file.

history.change: Acting GC rescinds GC 22-04 and more than a dozen other memos.

plain_summary: The Acting General Counsel rescinded GC 22-04 (the captive-audience memo) and more than a dozen other worker-friendly memos.
what_to_tell_workers: Every legal page shows its as-of date. Check "What's changed" before you rely on a rule.

history.change: NMB final rule: filing for an election needs a 50% showing of interest.
A majority of valid ballots cast decides the election (29 CFR 1202.4).

plain_summary: Airline and rail workers file for an NMB election with a 50% showing of interest; a majority of valid ballots cast decides.
what_to_tell_workers: Your bar to file is higher than under the NLRA (50%, not 30%). Aim for a big majority first.
